properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 24 at 11:16AM AKDT until October 26 at 7:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Coastal flooding, with water levels of 2.0 to 3.0 feet
above the normal highest tide line, and 40 mph southwest winds
with gusts up to 55 mph.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast, including Kipnuk, Kwigillingok
and Kongiganak.

* WHEN...7 PM Sunday to 7 AM AKDT Monday, highest water levels
expected around midnight Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Coastal flooding of low lying areas and erosion are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Relatively, the area to see higher water
levels is expected to be Kipnuk. The most likely scenario is for
water levels to be 2.0 to 3.0 ft above the normal high tide
line. Kwigillingok may see water levels of 1.0 to 2.0 ft above
the normal highest tide line. The peak will be around midnight
Monday morning, coinciding with high tide. Following this
system, steady southwesterly flow is expected to continue for
the Kuskokwim Delta coastline through Tuesday, which may slow
the ability for flood waters to recede.
properties.instruction:
A coastal flood advisory indicates that onshore winds and tides
will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 24 at 1:01PM MDT until October 24 at 5:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
FFWABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Eastern Cibola County in west central New Mexico...
East Central McKinley County in west central New Mexico...

* Until 500 PM MDT.

* At 101 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Up to 1 inch of rain has fallen.
Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the warned
area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Laguna Pueblo, Skyline-Ganipa, Acoma Pueblo, San Fidel, Cubero,
McCartys, New Laguna, Cebolletita and San Mateo.

This includes Interstate 40 between Mile Markers 92 and 114.
properties.instruction:
Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

In hilly or mountainous terrain there are numerous low water
crossings which are potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Find an
alternate route.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 5:00 PM MDT. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 5:00 PM MDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued October 24 at 2:16PM EDT until October 25 at 11:00AM EDT by NWS Charleston SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to 6 feet
in the surf zone. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to one
foot of inundation above ground level expected along shorelines
and tidal waterways (7.5 to 7.7 feet Mean Lower Low Water at
Charleston). For the Coastal Flood Watch, one to two feet of
inundation above ground level possible along shorelines and
tidal waterways (7.9 to 8.1 feet Mean Lower Low Water at
Charleston).

* WHERE...Coastal Colleton and Charleston Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday evening.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 5 PM EDT Monday. For the
Coastal Flood Advisory, until 10 PM EDT this evening. For the
Coastal Flood Watch, from late tonight through Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Significant saltwater inundation will render
numerous roads impassable. Properties may also flood.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tide will occur around 7:13 PM today
and around 7:34 AM Sunday at Charleston. Saltwater inundation
will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Visit water.weather.gov for additional water level and flood
impact information.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 4 and 12
inches.

* WHERE...Northern Susitna Valley, including Broad Pass.

* WHEN...From 1 PM this afternoon to 4 PM AKDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow will develop north of Talkeetna and
across Broad Pass by late this morning or early this afternoon. The
heaviest snow is expected to fall between late this evening and
Sunday morning before tapering off. The snow may mix with rain at
times near the south end of the pass, limiting snow accumulations.
After a break break in the snow, another round of snow is possible
overnight Sunday into early Monday morning.

conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor to moderate coastal flooding expected due to very
high tides.

* WHERE...Coastal areas of Los Angeles, Ventura, Santa Barbara,
and San Luis Obispo Counties.

* WHEN...From 5 AM Sunday to 1 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Minor to moderate flooding of sea water is likely
over vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the
time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike
paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach
erosion is likely. Isolated damage of structures due to sea
water inundation is possible to the most vulnerable areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides will likely reach 7.5-8.0 feet
(MLLW) each late morning, which is 1.0 to 1.5 feet above
astronomical projections. The highest tides will be Monday
through Wednesday. There is a small chance for isolated Coastal
Flood Warnings Wednesday through Thursday if larger surf
develops.
properties.instruction:

barricades or through water of unknown depth.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 24 at 12:42AM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA
properties.description:
Elevated fire weather conditions can be expected across portions
of southeast Louisiana and southern Mississippi this afternoon.
Relative humidity values are forecast to drop into the low 20 to
mid 30 percent range. The 20 ft wind forecast is expected to
remain at or below 10 mph, which should limit critical fire
weather conditions or at least the effective spread of fires that
may ignite.

Some improvement in humidity levels is expected on Sunday
afternoon with levels about 10 percent higher (30 to 40 percent)
than this afternoon. An additional 10 percent increase is possible
on Monday, which should lower the threat level somewhat.

Numerous local burn bans are in place and continue to expand across
LA and MS due to ongoing drought conditions. This now includes East
Feliciana, Iberville, Pointe Coupee, St. Helena, St Tammany,
Tangipahoa, Washington and West Feliciana Parishes along with
Wilkinson, Amite, Pike, and Walthall Counties. Regardless, outdoor
burning is strongly not recommended this afternoon, and all local
restrictions followed.

properties.areaDesc: Majuro Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 24 at 9:15AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
30W was upgraded to Tropical Storm In-fa over the northern Marshall
Islands at 700 AM ChST this morning, located near 10.6N 166.3E, or
120 miles north-northeast of Ujae Atoll, south of Bikini and Rongelap
Atolls. In-fa has maximum sustained winds of 40 mph, which extend
outward 115 miles to the southeast, 105 miles to the southwest, 100
miles to the northwest, and 40 miles to the northeast. This keeps
Ujae Atoll just outside the direct tropical storm-force wind field,
but strong sustained west to southwest winds with damaging tropical
storm-force gusts are expected through at least tonight as In-fa
begins to meander generally northward. The worst impacts will be
felt for islands and atolls across the northern and central Marshall
Islands, especially for west-facing exposures along the Ralik Chain,
such as Ujae, Enewetak, and Kwajalein Atolls. To the south of In-fa,
expect surging west to southwest winds of 20 to 30 knots with gusts
up to 45 knots, especially near heavier showers or outflow
boundaries. Boats should be safely secured away from west or south-
facing exposures, if possible. Significant boat damage has been
reported along west reefs already.

Seas will be hazardous to small craft throughout much of the central
and northern RMI, and dangerous within the tropical storm-force
winds closer to the center of In-fa. Do not attempt inter-island
travel. Even within the relatively calmer lagoon-side waters, inter-
island travel is strongly discouraged. Passing showers may produce
sudden strong to gale-force gusts, which will create locally
dangerous conditions. West to southwest swells will build to the
south of In- fa through the rest of the weekend, leading to elevated,
potentially hazardous surf along west- and south-facing reefs of the
central and northern RMI, mainly to the north and northwest of
Majuro.

Currently, In-fa is nearly-stationary, with its recent motion showing
a slight southeastward drift at around 1 mph, but is forecast to
begin slowly meandering north-northeast, then north-northwest through
this afternoon. Then, In-fa will see a slight increase in forward
speed through Sunday as it begins to exit the Marshall Islands. Winds
and seas will begin to ease through Sunday night, but sea conditions
may remain hazardous to small craft across the northern Marshalls
through Monday night. Light winds and a drier ridging pattern look to
set up across the region by the end of the week. This situation
will be closely monitored for additional impacts to the Marshall
Islands.

For more information on Tropical Storm In-fa, please refer to
bulletins from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header
WTPN31 PGTW and from the National Weather Service under WMO header
WTPQ31 PGUM.

flood damage.
